[LREG.2.1] Every match expression is legal in `where` only, never in `let`
([LREG.4.1]). The capture profile of its pattern determines which `where`
form it must use:

| Pattern shape | Required `where` form |
|---|---|
| One or more capturing groups | the capture-binding form, `where (name, ...) = ...` |
| Zero capturing groups | the plain boolean form, `where ... ~ /pattern/` |
| Negated (`!~`) | the plain boolean form |

The compiler must reject a `~` match expression on a `let`'s right-hand side,
whatever its capture profile, as `DS_VALIDATE_REGEX_CAPTURE_IN_LET`, with a message
that points the author at the `where` form the table names. A `!~` there is
[LREG.2.5]'s refusal instead.
